source_user: Give two failure modes or trade-offs associated with tensor parallelism. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Two important failure modes are collective timeout and per-rank out-of-memory. TP splits a layer across ranks, so each rank must participate in the required all-reduce, all-gather, or reduce-scatter; a slow or failed rank, fabric contention, or mismatched collective can stall the whole step. Separately, replicated activations, temporary buffers, padding, or an uneven partition can exceed one rank's memory even when aggregate capacity appears sufficient. Boundary: the exact failure behavior depends on the partition layout, runtime, topology, precision, and error-recovery policy. Reproduce with fixed layer shapes and workload, inspect rank logs and collective timelines, measure per-rank memory and failure rates, and verify output correctness before assigning cause.
risks: Collective failures and recovery semantics vary by runtime and fabric.
Aggregate memory can hide a single-rank OOM or imbalance.
evidence_required: Versioned model, layer shapes, precision, TP degree, topology, and runtime configuration.
Per-rank memory, collective timelines, logs, failure/recovery outcomes, and output-correctness checks.
Repeated runs with matched workload and documented uncertainty.

source_user: Give two failure modes or trade-offs associated with tensor parallelism. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Two trade-offs are communication overhead and load or memory imbalance. Each rank computes a shard of a layer and then waits for a collective to exchange or combine partial results; with small shards, a slow interconnect, or synchronization skew, collective time can dominate the saved local compute. An uneven partition or replicated temporary tensor can also leave one rank underutilized or out of memory. Boundary: TP can improve fit without improving speed, and the result is workload- and topology-specific. Hold model, precision, batch, sequence length, and runtime fixed, then measure per-rank memory, compute versus collective time, latency, throughput, errors, and output agreement.
risks: Communication cost depends on topology, collective implementation, and tensor shapes.
A capacity result must not be interpreted as a speedup without matched measurements.
evidence_required: Partition layout, rank count, layer dimensions, precision, topology, and runtime details.
Per-rank memory and compute/collective timing plus repeated latency and throughput measurements.
Failure logs and numerical/output-correctness comparisons.

source_user: Give two failure modes or trade-offs associated with tensor parallelism. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Two failure modes are (1) collective deadlock or timeout when ranks do not enter the same communication in the same order or the fabric is unhealthy, and (2) memory failure or severe imbalance when a partition leaves replicated buffers or temporary workspace concentrated on one rank. The mechanism is coordinated sharded computation: rank-local partial results cannot be consumed until the prescribed collective completes. Boundary: aggregate device memory is not a sufficient fit criterion; per-rank allocation, allocator fragmentation, topology, and runtime error handling determine the outcome. Test fixed shapes and loads, capture rank-level traces and memory high watermarks, record failure and recovery behavior, and check numerical equivalence.
risks: Deadlock and timeout diagnosis can be confounded by application or network faults.
Exact workspace and replication behavior is implementation-specific.
evidence_required: Collective ordering, rank logs, topology, runtime versions, and error-handling configuration.
Per-rank allocation traces, peak memory, utilization, failure rates, and recovery results.
Matched repeated tests with output-correctness checks.

source_user: Explain how tensor parallelism interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: TP partitions a layer's weights or intermediate dimensions across ranks. For a sharded matrix multiplication, ranks compute partial results and use a collective such as all-reduce or all-gather before dependent computation, reducing per-rank parameter or activation memory but adding synchronization and network traffic. Latency may fall if saved local work exceeds communication, while throughput can fall if collectives or imbalance dominate; capacity and speed are separate outcomes. Boundary: small batches, short sequences, unfavorable layer shapes, or a slow/contended fabric can make higher TP slower. Measure per-rank memory, compute/collective time, end-to-end latency, throughput, and output correctness for fixed workloads.
risks: The latency/throughput balance depends on phase, batching, topology, and kernel implementation.
Memory savings may be offset by replicated state or communication buffers.
evidence_required: Model dimensions, partition layout, precision, TP degree, topology, batch and sequence lengths.
Per-rank memory and phase/per-layer compute and collective timings.
Repeated end-to-end latency, throughput, failure, and correctness measurements.

source_user: Explain how tensor parallelism interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: In TP, each rank owns a shard of a layer and computes a local matrix-product contribution; a collective then combines or redistributes those contributions. This can reduce per-rank weight and activation memory and make an otherwise infeasible layer fit, but every synchronization adds communication and launch overhead. With sufficient arithmetic per shard it may improve throughput, whereas for latency-sensitive small requests the collective can increase tail latency and reduce throughput. Boundary: conclusions change with TP degree, interconnect, layer shape, batching, and whether the measured phase is prefill or decode. Compare matched configurations and report phase-specific p50/p95 latency, throughput, per-rank memory, and collective time.
risks: Tail latency is sensitive to queueing and collective stragglers, not just mean kernel time.
A fit improvement can be confounded by changing the total device budget.
evidence_required: TP layout, degree, hardware topology, runtime, phase, and matched request distributions.
Per-rank memory, collective/compute timelines, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and errors.
Repeated trials with output equivalence and uncertainty.

source_user: Explain how tensor parallelism interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Tensor parallelism distributes a layer's weights or activation dimensions, so each rank performs a smaller local operation and then participates in a collective required by the next layout. The split can lower per-rank model-state memory and permit larger models, but the collective consumes bandwidth and imposes a synchronization point. At large, well-utilized batches, saved computation may outweigh that cost; at small work sizes or with a slow fabric, latency and throughput can worsen, and memory may still be limited by replicated tensors and workspace. Boundary: do not generalize across TP degree, topology, precision, or prefill/decode phase. Measure those variables, per-rank memory, collective time, goodput, tail latency, and correctness.
risks: Communication and workspace behavior is backend-specific.
Large-batch throughput gains may not transfer to interactive tail latency.
evidence_required: Document partition layout, layer shapes, precision, TP degree, topology, batching, and phase.
Per-rank memory and compute/collective breakdown with latency, throughput/goodput, errors, and correctness.
Matched repeated workloads and uncertainty.

source_user: Explain how tensor parallelism interacts with latency, throughput, or memory. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: A TP linear layer may partition its input or output features: ranks compute local products, then an all-reduce or all-gather reconstructs the representation needed by the next operation. This reduces the local shard of weights and sometimes activation/workspace memory, but adds synchronization and cross-device bytes. Increasing TP can therefore improve fit and, for sufficiently large work, throughput; it can also increase latency or reduce throughput when communication, launch overhead, or rank imbalance dominates. Boundary: memory accounting and speed depend on the exact layout, replicated state, topology, batch, sequence length, and inference phase. Use per-rank telemetry and matched end-to-end measurements rather than utilization alone.
risks: Collective bytes and replicated tensors differ across row- and column-parallel layouts.
Utilization is not a causal explanation for latency or throughput changes.
evidence_required: Exact layer partition and collective schedule, model/precision, topology, TP degree, and workload.
Per-rank memory, traffic, compute/collective timing, latency, throughput, failures, and output checks.
Repeated matched baselines with uncertainty and phase separation.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether tensor parallelism helps a serving workload. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Define the serving workload first: model and revision, tokenizer, precision, prompt and output-length distributions, concurrency, arrival pattern, batching policy, SLO, and hardware topology. Compare a non-TP or lower-TP baseline only when it fits and keep software and resource conditions documented; sweep TP degrees that the topology supports. Confirm the mechanism with rank-local tensor shapes and collective traces around a sharded linear or attention operation. Warm up, repeat randomized trials, and record fit/admission failures, per-rank peak memory, compute versus collective time, TTFT, per-token and end-to-end latency (including p50/p95/p99), throughput/goodput, utilization, and output correctness. Boundary: a TP configuration that fits or raises throughput on this workload does not prove a universal speedup, especially if collective overhead dominates small requests.
risks: A baseline that uses a different device budget, kernel, or batching policy is not a clean performance comparison.
Queueing can obscure the per-request cost of collectives.
evidence_required: Immutable workload manifest, hardware/topology, software versions, TP layouts/degrees, and resource accounting.
Warmup/repetition protocol, per-rank memory and trace data, latency/throughput distributions, failures, and correctness.
Uncertainty estimates and explicit exclusion criteria for non-fitting baselines.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether tensor parallelism helps a serving workload. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Use a fixed, replayable request trace with prompt/output lengths, arrival rates, concurrency, and correctness criteria, and compare TP degrees under the same model, precision, runtime, and supported hardware conditions. For each condition, warm up, run repeated trials, and capture whether it fits, per-rank peak memory, rank imbalance, collective bytes and time, local compute time, queueing, TTFT, decode/token latency, p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, throughput, goodput, errors, and output agreement. Inspect a sharded matmul plus its all-reduce/all-gather to verify the mechanism. Boundary: if the no-TP baseline does not fit or uses a different device budget, report capacity separately and do not claim a speed comparison; small batches may be communication-bound. Record uncertainty and failed trials.
risks: Changing request mix or admission policy can change both queueing and apparent throughput.
Collective traces may require instrumentation overhead that should be controlled.
evidence_required: Versioned workload trace, model, precision, software, topology, TP layout/degree, and device budget.
Per-rank memory/imbalance and compute/collective/queueing telemetry plus latency distributions.
Repeated trial results, failures, uncertainty, and output-correctness verification.

source_user: Give a measurement plan for validating whether tensor parallelism helps a serving workload. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Tensor parallelism shards computation within layers and introduces collective communication; the best degree depends on memory, topology, batch, and communication cost.
corrected_answer: Establish a matched baseline and an explicit hypothesis: TP may reduce per-rank memory and local compute by partitioning a layer, but its all-reduce or all-gather can add synchronization. Freeze model revision, precision, runtime, kernels where comparable, topology, device count/budget, and a replayed request distribution; test several supported TP degrees with warmup and repeated trials. Trace one sharded operation and its collective, then collect per-rank memory and utilization, compute/communication/queueing time, admission and OOM failures, TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency percentiles, throughput/goodput, and output correctness. Boundary: a TP run that fits when the baseline does not supports a capacity finding, not a speedup claim; communication may dominate at small batch or sequence lengths. Report uncertainty and all exclusions.
risks: Instrumentation, kernel changes, and different device budgets can confound attribution.
Average throughput can hide tail-latency or failure-rate regressions.
evidence_required: Pre-registered workload, baseline eligibility rules, versions, topology, device budget, and TP configurations.
Rank-level trace/memory data and repeated latency, throughput, goodput, failure, and correctness measurements.
Confidence intervals or other uncertainty summary with failed/non-fitting conditions retained.
